claim: Israel deliberately targets civilians in Gaza, and the number of civilians killed proves it.

The organization considered the scale and severity of the casualties and destruction over time.

answer: Hamas and other armed groups are accused of operating among civilians in Gaza. What UN bodies documented is limited: weapons stored in vacant UN schools in 2014, and, in this war, only allegations. The UN human rights office also said Israel mostly did not substantiate its human-shield claims. The Israeli army's claim about tunnels under UNRWA's headquarters has not been independently verified. The law says a defender's violations do not release the attacker from its duties to civilians. A UN commission found that Israel's use of heavy weapons was an intentional attack on civilians, and the UN human rights office found repeated violations in six strikes; Israel rejects both. A parent can say: the evidence on each side is of different strength, and each strike has to be judged on its own facts.

facts.text: In the 2014 war, the UN Secretary-General and UNRWA reported weapons stored in vacant UN schools, which they condemned: UNRWA found about 20 rockets in one school in 2014 and, in 2020, a hand grenade and a military vest in another. The 2015 UN Commission of Inquiry also found that firing rockets from densely populated areas put Gazans in danger. These are documented by UN bodies themselves, but all trace to UN statements.

Israel's army says Hamas operates within densely populated areas, humanitarian zones, schools and hospitals; Hamas denies it.

UNRWA said it did not know what was underneath, had left the site on 12 October 2023, and called for an independent inquiry that it said was not possible during the war. Neither claim was independently verified in the coverage.

facts.text: The laws of war bind the attacker whatever the defender does. Additional Protocol I says that the presence of civilians must not be used to shield military objectives, and that a violation of that rule does not release the other party from its obligations to civilians, including precautions.

facts.text: Using civilians as human shields is prohibited. A US military manual says the party that uses human shields assumes responsibility for their injury, but the attacker may share it if it fails to take feasible precautions. West Point scholars add that targeting a whole area because tunnels are believed to lie beneath it could be indiscriminate.

Israel's army says it takes care to avoid harming civilians.

contested.text: Whether the number of dead proves intent: the law judges each attack by distinction, proportionality and precaution, and accepts that civilians may be harmed in attacks on military targets only within those limits (ICRC; West Point analysis). Amnesty infers intent from the scale and severity of casualties and destruction over time; the genocide question is on era5-genocide-claim.

could_not_verify: I looked for findings by Human Rights Watch, Amnesty or the UN Commission that Hamas used human shields in the 2023-2026 war and found only the UN human rights office's reports of 'allegations'. For the 2014 war the independent record is the UN Secretary-General's and UNRWA's own statements; the Amnesty and Human Rights Watch statements on that war are advocacy sources and are not counted.
The Israeli army's claim about the tunnels under UNRWA's headquarters was not independently verified in any source I could read; UNRWA said it did not know what was beneath the site.
The NATO Strategic Communications Centre of Excellence report on Hamas and human shields could not be read; it appears only as quoted by Lawfare, so I did not use it as a source.
Israel's reply to the June 2024 Commission report rests on AFP and UN News alone; I did not find a third independent report or the Israeli mission's own statement.

The OHCHR press release on the November 2024 verified-deaths report could not be fetched; the finding is cited from Al Jazeera, Reuters (via CBC) and LBC. LBC's quotation of the report on the army's evidence for human-shield claims has no second source.
I did not read the Israeli army's own investigations of individual strikes, or the Israeli mission's own statements.
not_claimed: This card does not say that Israel targets civilians, and does not say it does not; that is contested and has to be judged strike by strike.
It does not say that Hamas's conduct justifies civilian deaths or removes the attacker's duties.
It does not say that every report of Hamas operating from civilian places has been verified; some are allegations.
It does not say any particular strike was lawful or unlawful.

answer_claims.says: Hamas and other armed groups are accused of operating among civilians in Gaza.
What UN bodies documented is limited: weapons stored in vacant UN schools in 2014, and, in this war, only allegations.
The UN human rights office also said Israel mostly did not substantiate its human-shield claims.
The Israeli army's claim about tunnels under UNRWA's headquarters has not been independently verified.
The law says a defender's violations do not release the attacker from its duties to civilians.
A UN commission found that Israel's use of heavy weapons was an intentional attack on civilians, and the UN human rights office found repeated violations in six strikes; Israel rejects both.
A parent can say: the evidence on each side is of different strength, and each strike has to be judged on its own facts.

skeptic.notes: Read the OHCHR update and thematic report, ICRC statement, Lieber/West Point, Lawfare, UNRWA 2014 and 2020 statements, NPR/Jurist/AP on the UNRWA tunnels, RNZ/Reuters, Al Jazeera, Amnesty. Quotes are on the pages and the facts as worded hold. [must-fix] The card's claim is 'Israel deliberately targets civilians in Gaza, and the number killed proves it', but no fact tests it: the UN Commission of Inquiry's finding and the OHCHR report's finding (six strikes, 218 verified deaths, precaution 'consistently violated', and an IDF spokesperson reported as saying the focus is 'maximum damage' on the same page) and Israel's reply are only in contested, so the answer cannot carry them and reads as a defence of Israel's side. The writer must add facts for them, each with three reliable sources; the OHCHR thematic page and the Al Jazeera Commission report are already on the card. Strongest objection from critics of Israel (stronger): everything on the card for 'Hamas operates among civilians' is allegation (OHCHR's own word), a 2014 and 2020 UNRWA find in vacant schools, and an Israeli army claim about UNRWA tunnels that the card itself says was never verified; no finding from HRW, Amnesty or the Commission that Hamas used human shields in this war (the card's could_not_verify says so). Strongest objection from defenders: the answer leaves the UNRWA, tunnel and OHCHR 'allegation' evidence on equal footing with Commission findings and gives no weight to Hamas's stated tactics; I could not fix that from the cited pages. [should-fix] Fact 4 leans on one US-adviser commentary (Kittrie is a senior fellow at the Foundation for Defense of Democracies, an advocacy-leaning think tank, not stated on the card) for the human-shield rule; add the rule's primary source (Additional Protocol I art 51(7) or ICRC customary rule 97). [should-fix] Fact 0's third source (RNZ/Reuters) only reports Israel's claim and Hamas's denial; fact 1 is two UNRWA statements plus two outlets retelling the 2014 event, so one independent source. [nit] Lieber authors are US military law faculty; labelled scholarly, fine.

citer.notes: Removed: 'A UN commission and UN human rights office have found some Israeli attacks unlawful, and Israel rejects such findings.' No fact on the card carries it (the findings are only in contested/heard); the writer must add facts so it can return, and the answer is weaker without it. Reworded 'UNRWA found weapons in its own schools' to 'vacant schools it ran', which is what the two UNRWA statements say. The closing 'each strike has to be judged on its own facts' is carried by facts 3 and 4 (proportionality per attack; targeting a whole area could be indiscriminate). Converted 4 of 5 contested entries to {text, sources}; contested[4] ('Israel says it does not know how many civilians were killed (NBC)') has no source on this card and stays a string; the writer should point to era5-gaza-casualty-figures with a source or drop it. Dropped from contested[0] 'Israel rejects the Commission's findings' (no quote on the card).
